refuted.fact: Fact 6: 「API 的模型清單頁 Realtime 分類下只有 GPT-Live 1，沒有 mini 版」
refuted.why: The models catalogue page https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models has a section id="realtime" headed 'Realtime' / 'Models for realtime speech and translation' that lists SEVEN models, not one: gpt-live-1, gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, gpt-realtime-2, gpt-realtime-translate, gpt-realtime-1.5, gpt-realtime-mini. Two of those ARE mini models. The .md export of the same page is a flat alphabetical catalogue with no categories at all, so the claim cannot have come from the .md either. Only the narrower half is supportable: there is no gpt-live-1-mini anywhere in the API catalogue. As written the fact is false and it also contradicts the researcher's own fact 66 (Realtime is still being updated). Correct wording: 「API 模型清單沒有 gpt-live-1-mini。清單頁的 Realtime 區塊除了 GPT-Live 1，還列了 gpt-realtime-2.1、gpt-realtime-2.1-mini、gpt-realtime-2、gpt-realtime-translate、gpt-realtime-1.5、gpt-realtime-mini。」

BRIEF.md requires every date, price, percentage, plan name, region, language and model name to point at the text of one of the article's sources, so the pack cannot be written from this list. The researcher flagged it in sourcing_notes but left sources[] unchanged. Rebuild sources[] (max 4) around what the article actually says; guides/live-conversations and guides/your-data almost certainly have to replace two current entries.

unsupported.fact: Fact 16: gpt-6-astra 10.00/50.00 美元 ... 「這是 GPT-Live 後端可選模型的價格」
unsupported.why: The three price rows themselves are correct on the pricing page (gpt-5.6-terra $2.00/$12.00, gpt-5.6-luna $0.20/$1.20, gpt-6-astra $10.00/$50.00 short-context in/out). The ATTRIBUTION is not supported. The GPT-Live docs never publish a list of supported Responses-delegation backend models; guides/live-delegation names only GPT-5.6 Terra ('Start with') and GPT-5.6 Luna ('for cost-sensitive workloads'), and guides/live says only 'use a supported Responses model'. gpt-6-astra appears exactly once across every voice guide, at guides/voice-agents line 67, and that is inside the CHAINED voice pipeline Agents-SDK example, not a GPT-Live delegation example. Calling the gpt-6-astra price a GPT-Live backend price is inference.

additional_findings: MISSED and material, with a better first-party framing than the researcher used: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/audio (200; .md 200, 4,927 bytes) is OpenAI's own Audio and voice routing page and it now says 'For a new conversational voice application, start with GPT-Live', keeping Realtime for 'when you need its session and tool model'. That is a first-party positioning statement and is much stronger than inferring GPT-Live's status from the changelog. The researcher never fetched this page.

MISSED pricing caveat that is also a trap: pricing.md carries 'Regional processing (data residency) endpoints are charged a 10% uplift for models released on or after March 5, 2026, that are eligible for data residency.' GPT-Live 1 is data-residency eligible (US + EEA/Switzerland) and shipped after that date. BUT the note appears only under the Standard and Batch token tables and is NOT repeated in the 'GPT-Live sessions' block. So the article must NOT say the $0.05/min carries a 10% uplift; record it as 官方沒有對每分鐘費率說明是否適用.

MISSED first-party corroboration the article needs to sit correctly beside the existing 7/8 piece: the same official RSS carries 'Introducing GPT-Live', pubDate Wed, 08 Jul 2026 00:00:00 GMT (link /index/introducing-gpt-live), and 'How we built a realtime system for responsive voice AI in six months', Mon, 03 Aug 2026 (link /index/continuous-voice-interaction-with-gpt-live, also 403). The 7/8 pubDate is a first-party anchor for the 'ChatGPT 端兩個月前先推出' framing. Both article pages are 403, so only the feed metadata is usable.

MISSED, the concrete complement to fact 40: the partner table's own wording is Twilio = 'Connect incoming and outgoing phone calls to GPT-Live with Twilio Agent Connect' and Telnyx = 'Build outbound calling experiences with GPT-Live and the Telnyx Voice API'. That is what 'outbound must go through a partner integration' looks like in practice.

HAZARD for the writer (not a researcher error): guides/live-prompting says 'The live model has a small context window' while guides/live-conversations says 'The default context window holds 128,000 tokens'. Both are quoted correctly (facts 61 and 27) but placed in one article unexplained they read as self-contradiction. The reconciling numbers are also in the record: instructions cap at 16,384 tokens, startup history at 128 messages / 8,192 tokens, and the 128,000-token session window is consumed by audio tokens that never appear in the transcript.

not_said[] audited and accurate. I grepped every GPT-Live guide plus the model page for language lists, eligibility gating, watermark/SynthID, SLA and duration limits. There is no spoken-language list anywhere; no waitlist or eligibility gate for GPT-Live itself (gating exists only for SIP enablement, session storage and custom voices); no watermark and no AI-disclosure requirement (the docs only show how to REQUEST a spoken disclosure and warn it is not guaranteed verbatim); no SLA; and no number for the session duration limit behind session.closed reason 'expired'. The must-not-write list is sound; the only addition is the 10% data-residency uplift trap above.

event_date 2026-09-10 stands. RSS pubDate Thu, 10 Sep 2026 and the changelog 'Sep 10' heading agree, GA is stated as a state with no separate availability date or rollout schedule, and no announcement/publication/effective/availability conflation exists in the record. Vendor claims are correctly flagged: facts 1, 7 and 8 are the only is_vendor_claim=true entries and they are exactly the three adjectival OpenAI statements ('stronger instruction following', 'full-duplex voice model ... delegate reasoning', 'Our premier model ... smooth interruption handling'). I found no vendor claim recorded as independent fact.
